proposals.value: As AI shifts from models to deployment, who captures the value—and who bears the costs?
proposals.evidence: Evolves current question 'Who can deploy AI at scale—and who benefits?' by merging the deployment thesis (CL-PLATFORM: source-002, source-004; CL-INFRA: source-009) with the value-accrual question (CL-ECON: source-010, source-011, source-012) and the distribution-of-burden lens (CL-HUMAN: source-013, source-015). 14 words, action-oriented.

proposals.value: The AI race is no longer decided by the smartest model. Platform thinkers argue the agent layer and default interfaces will capture users and value (5-article cluster CL-PLATFORM); infrastructure coverage insists chips, power and data centers set the real ceiling on who can compete (CL-INFRA); and economics coverage asks why falling inference prices have not yet produced a clear winner in the value chain (CL-ECON). Meanwhile the fastest-growing lens is human impact: labor, classrooms and creative credit are becoming the tests of whether the race produces public value or private displacement (CL-HUMAN). The central uncertainty has moved from capability to consequence: where durable advantage settles, and who pays for it.
proposals.evidence: Synthesis references 4 distinct perspectives with cluster-level evidence: CL-PLATFORM (5 articles), CL-INFRA (3), CL-ECON (3), CL-HUMAN (3), plus CL-TECH framing shift (source-001).
